red.definition: The colour seen in ripe strawberries and many tomatoes.
red.exampleUsage: The ripe apples on the tree turned a bright red.

blue.definition: The color of a clear daytime sky and the deep ocean.
blue.exampleUsage: The sky was clear and blue above the mountain peaks.

yellow.definition: The colour of ripe lemons and sunflower petals.
yellow.exampleUsage: Bright yellow sunflowers bloomed along the garden fence.

green.definition: The colour of many fresh leaves and blades of grass.
green.exampleUsage: After the spring rain, the hills were covered in green grass.

orange.definition: The warm color between red and yellow, like carrots and citrus fruit.
orange.exampleUsage: The setting sun painted the clouds in shades of orange.

purple.definition: A colour between red and blue, seen in some flowers.
purple.exampleUsage: She chose a deep purple cover for her notebook.

pink.definition: A pale, soft shade of red, like spring blossoms and rose petals.
pink.exampleUsage: The cherry trees were covered in soft pink blossoms.

brown.definition: The natural earthy color of tree bark, soil, coffee beans, and wood.
brown.exampleUsage: The carpenter polished the warm brown surface of the oak table.

black.definition: The darkest color, like charcoal, ink, or a moonless night sky.
black.exampleUsage: He wrote the title neatly in black ink.

white.definition: The lightest color, like fresh snow, milk, or clean cotton.
white.exampleUsage: He wore a clean white shirt to Friday prayer.

cyan.definition: A bright greenish-blue color used in printing and digital screens.
cyan.exampleUsage: The printer needed a new cyan ink cartridge.

magenta.definition: A vivid purplish-red color used as a primary ink color in printing.
magenta.exampleUsage: The desert flowers bloomed in a striking shade of magenta.

lime.definition: A bright, fresh yellowish-green color like the skin of a lime fruit.
lime.exampleUsage: The sports jersey had bright lime stripes along the sleeves.

teal.definition: A medium to deep blue-green color.
teal.exampleUsage: The ceramic tiles in the courtyard were glazed in deep teal.

indigo.definition: A deep, rich blue-purple color between blue and violet in the spectrum.
indigo.exampleUsage: At dusk, the evening sky darkened to a deep indigo.

violet.definition: A bluish-purple color at the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum.
violet.exampleUsage: Small violet wildflowers grew beside the mountain stream.

coral.definition: A warm pinkish-orange color named after sea coral.
coral.exampleUsage: The seashell had a smooth coral tint on the inside.

salmon.definition: A soft pinkish-orange color resembling the flesh of salmon fish.
salmon.exampleUsage: The morning clouds glowed with a soft salmon hue at dawn.

turquoise.definition: A bright greenish-blue color named after the turquoise gemstone.
turquoise.exampleUsage: The shallow water near the coast was a clear turquoise.

lavender.definition: A pale, gentle purple color with a cool bluish tone, like lavender flowers.
lavender.exampleUsage: The bedroom curtains were a soft shade of lavender.

light.definition: Pale or closer to white in colour, rather than dark.
light.exampleUsage: Painting the walls light blue made the small room feel larger.

dark.definition: Deep in color and closer to black than to white.
dark.exampleUsage: He wore a dark gray coat during the winter trip.

bright.definition: Strong and vivid in colour in this context.
bright.exampleUsage: Road workers wear bright yellow vests so drivers can see them.

dull.definition: Softened or muted in color, lacking brightness or shine.
dull.exampleUsage: Over time, the old brass lamp turned a dull brown.

vivid.definition: Intensely rich, clear, and strong in color.
vivid.exampleUsage: The artist used vivid greens and blues to paint the oasis.

pale.definition: Very light and soft in color, with only a gentle hint of hue.
pale.exampleUsage: The baby's blanket was knitted from pale yellow wool.

deep.definition: Rich, strong, and dark in color tone.
deep.exampleUsage: The library carpet was woven in a deep emerald green.

warm.definition: Describing a colour group that includes red, orange and yellow.
warm.exampleUsage: Warm earth tones like ochre and brown make a room feel welcoming.

cool.definition: Describing a colour group that includes blue and many greens.
cool.exampleUsage: The designer used cool blues and grays for the study room.

neutral.definition: Describing understated colours such as grey, beige, white or black.
neutral.exampleUsage: Neutral colors like beige and gray match almost any furniture.

mix.definition: To combine two or more colours or paints together.
mix.exampleUsage: Rana will mix the two paints on her palette.

blend.definition: To transition or merge two colors smoothly so there is no sharp line between them.
blend.exampleUsage: Use a soft brush to blend the sky colors from blue to gold.

shade.definition: A darker version of a color made by adding black, or a specific variation of a color.
shade.exampleUsage: The artist used a darker shade of green for the pine trees.

tint.definition: A lighter variation of a color created by mixing it with white.
tint.exampleUsage: Adding white paint to red creates a soft pink tint.

hue.definition: The colour type, such as red, yellow, green or blue.
hue.exampleUsage: In autumn, the maple leaves turn a golden hue.

saturation.definition: How strong or intense a colour is, rather than muted.
saturation.exampleUsage: Lowering saturation makes the blue less intense.

gradient.definition: A smooth, gradual transition from one color or shade to another.
gradient.exampleUsage: The poster background features a smooth gradient from navy to sky blue.

rainbow.definition: An arch of colors seen when sunlight passes through water droplets.
rainbow.exampleUsage: After the rainstorm, a bright rainbow appeared over the valley.

spectrum.definition: The complete band of colors produced when white light is separated by a prism.
spectrum.exampleUsage: A glass prism splits sunlight into the full visible spectrum.

pigment.definition: A coloured material used to give paint or ink its colour.
pigment.exampleUsage: Traditional painters ground lapis lazuli stone to make blue pigment.
